```{r}
library(dplyr)
```

# 1. Data loading

```{r}
ifood_df <- read.csv("data.csv")
```

# 2. Preprocessing

## 2.1. Duplicates

There are 2 kinds of duplicated entries in this dataset:

\- same response across duplicates;

\- different response across duplicates.

In the first case we will keep one and delete the remaining duplicates.
In the second case we will delete all of them.

```{r}
ifood_df <- ifood_df %>%
  group_by(across(-c(ID,Response))) %>%
  filter(!(n() > 1 & n_distinct(Response) > 1)) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup()

ifood_df <- as.data.frame(ifood_df)
nrow(ifood_df)
```

## 2.2. Data Transformation and Feature Engineering

The main data transformations and feature engineering steps were: the
customer join date was converted into the number of days as as customer,
the birth year was transformed into age, aggregated variables such as
total purchases and total accepted campaigns were created, and
unnecessary columns were removed or reordered to improve data usability.

```{r}
# Convert Dt_Customer to proper Date format
ifood_df$Dt_Customer <- ymd(ifood_df$Dt_Customer)

# Find reference date = max(Dt_Customer) + 100 days
ref_date <- max(ifood_df$Dt_Customer, na.rm = TRUE) + days(100)

# Create Customer Age Column
ifood_df <- ifood_df %>%
  mutate(Age = year(ref_date) - Year_Birth)

# Number of days as a customer using ref_date
ifood_df <- ifood_df %>%
  mutate(Customer_Days = as.numeric(difftime(ref_date, Dt_Customer, units = "days")))

# Drop unused columns
ifood_df <- ifood_df %>%
  dplyr::select(-ID, -Year_Birth, -Dt_Customer,-Z_CostContact,-Z_Revenue)

# Sum of purchases
ifood_df <- ifood_df %>%
  mutate(MntTotal = MntWines + MntFruits + MntMeatProducts + MntFishProducts + MntSweetProducts)

# Sum of accepted campaigns
ifood_df$TotalCmp <- rowSums(ifood_df[, c("AcceptedCmp1","AcceptedCmp2","AcceptedCmp3","AcceptedCmp4","AcceptedCmp5")])

# Move Age to the first position
ifood_df <- ifood_df %>%
  relocate(Age, .before = 1)

# Move Customer_Days to be right before Recency
ifood_df <- ifood_df %>%
  relocate(Customer_Days, .before = Recency)

ifood_df <- ifood_df %>%
  relocate(MntTotal, .before = NumDealsPurchases)

ifood_df <- ifood_df %>%
  relocate(TotalCmp, .before = Complain)
```

## 2.3. Handling non-compliant / inconsistent responses

### 2.3.1. Marital Status

```{r}
# Marital -> Replace certain values with "Single"
ifood_df$Marital_Status[ifood_df$Marital_Status %in% c("Alone", "Absurd", "YOLO")] <- "Single"
```

### 2.3.2. Income

```{r}
# Filter matching entries (excluding row 1505)
matching_group <- ifood_df %>%
  filter(Education == "Graduation",
         Marital_Status == "Together",
         Age >= 30,
         Age <= 50,
         row_number() != 1505)
mean_income <- mean(matching_group$Income, na.rm = TRUE)

# Update Income in row 1505
ifood_df$Income[1505] <- round(mean_income)

nrow(matching_group)
round(mean_income)
```

### 2.3.3. Age

```{r}
matching_group <- ifood_df %>%
  filter(Education == "2n Cycle",
         Marital_Status == "Single",
         row_number() != 1)
mean_age <- mean(matching_group$Age, na.rm = TRUE)

ifood_df$Age[1] <- round(mean_age)

nrow(matching_group)
round(mean_age)

matching_group <- ifood_df %>%
  filter(Education == "PhD",
         Marital_Status == "Together",
         row_number() != 2)
mean_age <- mean(matching_group$Age, na.rm = TRUE)

ifood_df$Age[2] <- round(mean_age)

nrow(matching_group)
round(mean_age)

matching_group <- ifood_df %>%
  filter(Education == "2n Cycle",
         Marital_Status == "Divorced",
         row_number() != 3)
mean_age <- mean(matching_group$Age, na.rm = TRUE)

ifood_df$Age[3] <- round(mean_age)

nrow(matching_group)
round(mean_age)
```

## 2.4. Missing Values

```{r}
data.frame(
  Column = names(ifood_df),
  Missing_Values = colSums(is.na(ifood_df))
)
```

We substituted them according to the demographic's mean - Same
Education - Same Marital Status - ±10 years of age.

```{r}
# Replace missing Income values
ifood_df <- ifood_df %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    Income = ifelse(
      is.na(Income),
      {
        # Get current row values
        curr_edu <- Education
        curr_mari <- Marital_Status
        curr_age <- Age

        # Filter matching rows from dataset (excluding current)
        mean_income <- ifood_df %>%
          filter(Education == curr_edu,
                 Marital_Status == curr_mari,
                 Age >= curr_age - 10,
                 Age <= curr_age + 10,
                 !is.na(Income)) %>%
          summarise(mean_income = mean(Income, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
          pull(mean_income)

        # Convert final value to integer
        as.integer(mean_income)
        print(as.integer(mean_income))
      },
      Income
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

ifood_df <- as.data.frame(ifood_df)
```

# 3. Explanatory Data Analysis (EDA)

What does the average customer look like for this company? Which
marketing campaign was most successful? Which products are performing
best? Which channels are underperforming?

## 3.1. Target Variable Overview

```{r}
prop.table(table(ifood_df$Response)) 
# Unbalanced
cost_FP <- 3
gain_TP <- 8

response_rate <- mean(ifood_df$Response == 1) #P(Y=1)
response_rate
profit_contact_all <- response_rate * gain_TP - cost_FP
profit_contact_all 
total_profit_contact_all <- profit_contact_all * nrow(ifood_df)
total_profit_contact_all
ggplot(ifood_df, aes(x = as.factor(Response))) +
  geom_bar(aes(y = after_stat(count / sum(count) * 100)),
           fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(round(after_stat(count / sum(count) * 100), 1), "%"),
    y = after_stat(count / sum(count) * 100)),
    stat = "count",
    vjust = -0.5
  ) +
  labs(
    y = "Percentage of customers (%)",
    x = "Campaign response",
    title = "Campaign response distribution"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0, 100)) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### 3.2.4. Average Customer Profile

```{r}
ifood_df %>%
  group_by(Education) %>%
  summarise(resp_rate = mean(Response),
            Perc = n()/nrow(ifood_df)) %>%  #most are graduate, the more educated higher the acceptance
  arrange(desc(resp_rate))

ifood_df %>%
  group_by(Marital_Status) %>%
  summarise(resp_rate = mean(Response),
            Perc = n()/nrow(ifood_df)) %>%  #most are in a relationship (married or together), people that aren't in a relationship (single, divorced and widow) have a higher acceptance
  arrange(desc(resp_rate))

ifood_df %>%
  group_by(Kidhome) %>%
  summarise(resp_rate = mean(Response),
            Perc = n()/nrow(ifood_df)) %>% #most people have 1 or no children and people with fewer children have a higher acceptance
  arrange(desc(resp_rate))

ifood_df %>%
  group_by(Teenhome) %>%
  summarise(resp_rate = mean(Response),
            Perc = n()/nrow(ifood_df)) %>% #most have 1 or none teen and people with no teens are more likely to accept
  arrange(desc(resp_rate))

ifood_df %>%
  group_by(Complain) %>%
  summarise(resp_rate = mean(Response),
            Perc = n()/nrow(ifood_df)) %>% #almost no one made a complain. This most likely is not a good discriminative feature for that reason: the response rate for the ones who complain is not viable
  arrange(desc(resp_rate))

ifood_df %>%
  group_by(TotalCmp) %>%
  summarise(resp_rate = mean(Response),
            Perc = n()/nrow(ifood_df)) %>% #the majority of the customers don't accept the campaigns. A customer who tends to accept the prior campaigns is more likely to accept this one
  arrange(desc(resp_rate))
```

```{r}
ifood_df %>%
  group_by(Response) %>%
  summarise(
    n          = n(),
    mean_income = mean(Income, na.rm = TRUE), #more money->accept
    median_income = median(Income), #non responsers not skewed
    mean_mnttotal = mean(MntTotal), #spend more money ->accept
    median_mnttotal = median(MntTotal), #skewed, most people don't spend huge amounts of money
    mean_age   = mean(Age), #not a strong discriminative power
    median_age = median(Age),
    mean_recency  = mean(Recency), #customers that bought something recently tend to accept
    median_recency = median(Recency), #not skewed
    mean_customer_days = mean(Customer_Days), #loyalty helps
    median_customer_days = median(Customer_Days)
  )
```

## 3.3. Marketing Campaign Performance

### 3.3.1. Campaign Acceptance Rates

```{r}
campaign_summary <- ifood_df %>%
    summarise(
      response_rate = mean(Response==1, na.rm=TRUE),
      across(starts_with("AcceptedCmp"), ~mean(.==1, na.rm=TRUE), .names = "rate_{col}")
    ) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to="metric", values_to="value")
  campaign_summary
  # Plot (accepted campaigns rates)
  ifood_df %>%
    dplyr::select(starts_with("AcceptedCmp")) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to="cmp", values_to="accepted") %>%
    group_by(cmp) %>%
    summarise(rate = mean(accepted==1, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x=fct_reorder(cmp, rate), y=rate)) +
    geom_col() + scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) + coord_flip() +
    labs(title="Acceptance rate by Campaign", y="Acceptance rate", x="Campaign")+
    theme_minimal()
# There is no campaign that stands out for high acceptance and campaign 2 was very low compared to the others
```

## 3.6. Response Analysis by Demographics

```{r}
# Frequency of each marital status

# Frequency table: one row per Marital_Status
freq_df <- ifood_df %>%
  count(Marital_Status) %>%
  mutate(width = n / sum(n)) %>%
  arrange(Marital_Status) %>%
  mutate(
    xmin = lag(cumsum(width), default = 0),
    xmax = cumsum(width),
    xmid = (xmin + xmax) / 2
  )

plot_df <- ifood_df %>%
  count(Marital_Status, Response) %>%
  group_by(Marital_Status) %>%
  mutate(
    p = n / sum(n),
    cum = cumsum(p),
    ymax = 1 - lag(cum, default = 0),

  ) %>%
  left_join(freq_df, by = "Marital_Status")
```

# 4. Predictive Modeling

## 4.1. Data Preparation for Modeling

### 4.1.1. Response Variable Encoding

```{r}
ifood_df$Response <- factor(ifood_df$Response, levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No","Yes"))
```

### 4.1.2. Train-Validation-Test Split

```{r}
set.seed(333)
sample <- createDataPartition(ifood_df$Response, p = 0.6, list = FALSE)
train <- ifood_df[sample, ]
rest <- ifood_df[-sample, ]

idx_val <- createDataPartition(rest$Response, p = 0.375, list = FALSE)
val  <- rest[idx_val, ]
test <- rest[-idx_val, ]
```

### 4.1.3. Class Proportion Verification

```{r}
prop.table(table(train$Response))
prop.table(table(val$Response))
prop.table(table(test$Response))
```

### 4.1.4. Cross-Validation Strategy

```{r}
ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 10,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,   # compute ROC
  savePredictions = TRUE
)
```

## 4.2. Feature Encoding and Scaling

### 4.2.1. Dummy Encoding of Categorical Variables

```{r}
X_train <- train[, !colnames(train) %in% "Response"]

# Convert Education and Marital_Status into dummy variables
X_train_num <- dummy_cols(
  X_train, 
  select_columns = c("Education", "Marital_Status"), 
  remove_selected_columns = TRUE,   # removes original char columns
  remove_first_dummy = TRUE         # avoids multicollinearity
)

X_val_num <- dummy_cols(
  val[, !colnames(val) %in% "Response"],
  select_columns = c("Education","Marital_Status"),
  remove_selected_columns = TRUE,
  remove_first_dummy = TRUE
)

X_test_num <- dummy_cols(
  test[, !colnames(test) %in% "Response"],
  select_columns = c("Education","Marital_Status"),
  remove_selected_columns = TRUE,
  remove_first_dummy = TRUE
)
```

### 4.2.2. Feature Scaling

```{r}
train_scaled <- scale(X_train_num)
val_scaled <- scale(
  X_val_num,
  center = attr(train_scaled, "scaled:center"),
  scale  = attr(train_scaled, "scaled:scale")
)

test_scaled <- scale(
  X_test_num,
  center = attr(train_scaled, "scaled:center"),
  scale  = attr(train_scaled, "scaled:scale")
)
```

```{r}
final_model <- glm(
  Response ~ . -MntMeatProducts -MntFishProducts -MntSweetProducts -MntWines -MntFruits -
    AcceptedCmp1 -AcceptedCmp2 -AcceptedCmp3 -AcceptedCmp4 -AcceptedCmp5,
  family = "binomial",
  data = train
)

car::vif(final_model)
```

### 4.3.4. Profit-Based Threshold Optimization (Validation Set)

```{r}
pred_val <- predict(final_model, val, type="response")

gain_TP <- 8
cost_FP <- 3

ths <- seq(0, 1, by=0.001)

compute_profit <- function(th){
  pred_class <- ifelse(pred_val >= th, "Yes", "No")
  sum(ifelse(pred_class=="Yes" & val$Response=="Yes",  gain_TP,
      ifelse(pred_class=="Yes" & val$Response=="No", -cost_FP, 0)))
}

profits <- sapply(ths, compute_profit)

best_cutoff_profit <- ths[which.max(profits)]
best_cutoff_profit
```

### 4.3.5. Logistic Regression Performance on Test Set

```{r}
predicted <- predict(final_model, test, type="response")
roc_obj <- roc(test$Response, predicted)

auc(roc_obj)
```

```{r}
conf_mat

total_profit
```

## 4.6. PCA + Logistic Regression

### 4.6.1. Estimation

```{r}
#Select the numerical variables (excluding Response)

pca_vars_train <- train %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Age, Income, Kidhome, Teenhome, Recency,
    MntWines, MntFruits, MntMeatProducts, MntFishProducts,
    MntSweetProducts, MntGoldProds, MntTotal,
    NumDealsPurchases, NumWebPurchases, NumCatalogPurchases,
    NumStorePurchases, NumWebVisitsMonth, Customer_Days,
    TotalCmp
  )

# Fit PCA ONLY on training predictors (prevents data leakage)
pca_res <- prcomp(pca_vars_train, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Summary (variance explained)
summary(pca_res)
```

### 4.6.2. Choose number of PC's

```{r}
eigval   <- (pca_res$sdev)^2
prop_var <- eigval / sum(eigval)
cum_var  <- cumsum(prop_var)

k_80    <- which(cum_var >= 0.80)[1]
k_90    <- which(cum_var >= 0.90)[1]
k_kaiser <- sum(eigval >= 1)

cat("=== PCA retention criteria (TRAIN PCA) ===\n")
cat("k (>=80% variance):", k_80, " | CumVar =", round(cum_var[k_80]*100, 2), "%\n")
cat("k (>=90% variance):", k_90, " | CumVar =", round(cum_var[k_90]*100, 2), "%\n")
cat("k (Kaiser eig>=1):", k_kaiser, " | CumVar =", round(cum_var[k_kaiser]*100, 2), "%\n\n")

k <- k_kaiser

#Scree plot
scree_df <- data.frame(
  PC = seq_along(eigval),
  Variance = prop_var,
  CumVar = cum_var
)

ggplot(scree_df, aes(x = PC, y = Variance)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Scree plot (proportion of variance explained)",
    x = "Principal Component",
    y = "Proportion of variance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### 4.6.3. Interpretation of PCs

```{r}
#Interpret PCs via loadings

top_loadings <- function(rotation_mat, pc, top_n) {
  v <- rotation_mat[, pc]
  out <- sort(abs(v), decreasing = TRUE)[1:top_n]
  data.frame(
    Variable = names(out),
    Loading = rotation_mat[names(out), pc],
    AbsLoading = out,
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

rotation <- pca_res$rotation

cat("=== Top loadings (PC1) ===\n")
print(top_loadings(rotation, pc = 1, top_n = 8))
cat("\n=== Top loadings (PC2) ===\n")
print(top_loadings(rotation, pc = 2, top_n = 8))
cat("\n=== Top loadings (PC3) ===\n")
print(top_loadings(rotation, pc = 3, top_n = 8))
cat("\n=== Top loadings (PC4) ===\n")
print(top_loadings(rotation, pc = 4, top_n = 8))
cat("\n=== Top loadings (PC5) ===\n")
print(top_loadings(rotation, pc = 5, top_n = 8))

#PCA plots

#Variables factor map
fviz_pca_var(pca_res, col.var = "contrib") +
  labs(title = "PCA – Variable contributions (PC1 vs PC2)")

# Individuals factor map by Response
resp_factor <- as.factor(train$Response)

fviz_pca_ind(
  pca_res,
  geom = "point",
  habillage = resp_factor,
  addEllipses = TRUE,
  ellipse.level = 0.95
) + labs(title = "PCA – Individuals (colored by Response)")
```

### 4.6.4. Model Training

```{r}

k <- 9

# Project TRAIN / VAL / TEST onto the PCA space learned from TRAIN
PC_train <- as.data.frame(predict(pca_res, newdata = pca_vars_train)[, 1:k, drop = FALSE])
PC_train$Response <- factor(train$Response, levels = c("No", "Yes"))

pca_vars_val <- val %>%
  dplyr::select(names(pca_vars_train))
PC_val <- as.data.frame(predict(pca_res, newdata = pca_vars_val)[, 1:k, drop = FALSE])
PC_val$Response <- factor(val$Response, levels = c("No", "Yes"))

pca_vars_test <- test %>%
  dplyr::select(names(pca_vars_train))
PC_test <- as.data.frame(predict(pca_res, newdata = pca_vars_test)[, 1:k, drop = FALSE])
PC_test$Response <- factor(test$Response, levels = c("No", "Yes"))

# Fit logistic model on PCs
model_pca <- glm(Response ~ ., data = PC_train, family = binomial)
pscl::pR2(model_pca)["McFadden"]

```

### 4.6.5. Profit-based cutoff selection

```{r}
pred_pca_val <- predict(model_pca, newdata = PC_val, type = "response")

gain_TP <- 8
cost_FP <- 3

ths <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.001)

compute_profit <- function(th) {
  pred_class <- ifelse(pred_pca_val >= th, "Yes", "No")
  pred_class <- factor(pred_class, levels = c("No", "Yes"))
  y_true <- PC_val$Response

  sum(ifelse(pred_class == "Yes" & y_true == "Yes",  gain_TP,
      ifelse(pred_class == "Yes" & y_true == "No",  -cost_FP, 0)))
}

profits <- sapply(ths, compute_profit)
best_cutoff_profit_pca <- ths[which.max(profits)]
best_cutoff_profit_pca

```

```{r}
roc_obj_pca <- pROC::roc(PC_test$Response, predicted_pca)
plot(roc_obj_pca, print.auc = TRUE, legacy.axes = TRUE)
roc_obj_pca$auc

conf_matrix_pca

              ifelse(pred_class_pca == "Yes" & PC_test$Response == "No",  -3, 0))
total_profit_pca <- sum(profit_pca)
total_profit_pca
```

### 4.8.5. Hyperparameter grid search (validation profit)

```{r}
grid <- expand.grid(
  num.trees = c(100, 500, 700, 1000),
  mtry = c(3,4,5, 6, 7,8,9),
  min.node.size = c(5, 10,15, 20)
)

results <- data.frame()

for(i in 1:nrow(grid)){
  rf_tmp <- ranger(
    Response ~ .-MntMeatProducts -MntWines -MntFishProducts -MntSweetProducts  -MntFruits -
    AcceptedCmp1 -AcceptedCmp2 -AcceptedCmp3 -AcceptedCmp4 -AcceptedCmp5,
    data = train,
    probability = TRUE,
    num.trees = grid$num.trees[i],
    mtry = grid$mtry[i],
    min.node.size = grid$min.node.size[i]
  )
  
  pred_val <- predict(rf_tmp, data = val)$predictions[,"Yes"]
  
  profit <- max(sapply(ths, function(th){
    pred_class <- ifelse(pred_val >= th, "Yes", "No")
    sum(ifelse(pred_class=="Yes" & y_val=="Yes", 8,
               ifelse(pred_class=="Yes" & y_val=="No", -3, 0)))
  }))
  
  results <- rbind(results,
    data.frame(mtry = grid$mtry[i],
               min.node.size = grid$min.node.size[i],
               num.trees = grid$num.trees[i],
               profit = profit)
  )
}

results
```

```{r}
                        ifelse(pred_class_all_rf == "Yes" & ifood_df$Response == "No", -3, 0))

total_profit_all_rf <- sum(profit_all_rf)
total_profit_all_rf
mean_profit_all_rf <- mean(profit_all_rf)
mean_profit_all_rf
mean(pred_class_all_rf == "Yes")
```


## 4.9. Multilayer Perceptron

### 4.9.1 Hyperparameter search

```{r}
library(nnet)
set.seed(2025)

# using random search to tune hyperparameters
param_grid <- list(
  size = sample(5:64, 50, replace = TRUE),      # hidden units
  decay = runif(50, 0, 0.1),                    # weight decay
  maxit = sample(c(100, 200, 500), 50, replace = TRUE)
)

results <- data.frame(size = integer(),
                      decay = numeric(),
                      maxit = integer(),
                      bal_acc = numeric())


# 5-fold cv sorted by mean profit
k <- 5
folds <- sample(rep(1:k, length.out = nrow(train)))

for (i in 1:length(param_grid$size)) {
  print(i)

  size_i <- param_grid$size[i]
  decay_i <- param_grid$decay[i]
  maxit_i <- param_grid$maxit[i]
  cv_results <- numeric(k)
  for (j in 1:k) {

    train_idx <- which(folds != j)
    m_train <- X_train_num[train_idx,]
    val_idx   <- which(folds == j)
    m_val <- X_train_num[val_idx,]
    
    m_train <- scale(m_train)
    m_val <- scale(
      m_val,
      center = attr(m_train, "scaled:center"),
      scale  = attr(m_train, "scaled:scale")
    )
    
    m_train <- as.data.frame(m_train)
    m_val   <- as.data.frame(m_val)
    
    colnames(m_train) <- colnames(X_train_num)
    colnames(m_val)   <- colnames(X_train_num)
  
    m_train$Response <- train[train_idx,]$Response
    m_val$Response <- train[val_idx,]$Response

    model <- nnet(Response ~ .-MntMeatProducts -MntWines -MntFishProducts -MntSweetProducts  -MntFruits, data = m_train, size = size_i, decay = decay_i, maxit = maxit_i, trace = FALSE, MaxNWts = 2000)

        prob <- predict(model, m_val,type = "raw")

    predictions <- ifelse(prob > 3/11, 1L, 0L)
    true <- ifelse(m_val$Response == "Yes", 1L, 0L)

    p <- sum(predictions * (11 * true - 3))

    cv_results[j] <- p
  }
  p_mean = sum(cv_results)/5
  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(size = size_i, decay = decay_i,
                                         maxit = maxit_i, profit = p_mean))
}

# Sort results by profit
results <- results %>% arrange(desc(profit))
print(results)

```

```{r}
m_test$Response <- test$Response
```

### 4.9.3 Empirical cutoff

```{r}
set.seed(2025)
# empirical cutoff

pred_val <- predict(model, m_val, type="raw")
true <- ifelse(m_val$Response == "Yes", 1L, 0L)

gain_TP <- 8
cost_FP <- 3

ths <- seq(0, 1, by=0.001)

compute_profit_mlp <- function(th){
  pred_class <- ifelse(pred_val >= th, 1, 0)
  sum(ifelse(pred_class==1 & true==1,  gain_TP,
      ifelse(pred_class==1 & true==0, -cost_FP, 0)))
}

profits_mlp <- sapply(ths, compute_profit_mlp)

best_cutoff_profit_mlp <- ths[which.max(profits_mlp)]
best_cutoff_profit_mlp

prob <- predict(model, m_test, type = "raw")
    
predictions <- ifelse(prob > best_cutoff_profit_mlp, 1L, 0L)
true <- ifelse(m_test$Response == "Yes", 1L, 0L)

p <- sum(predictions * (11 * true - 3))

conf_mat <- confusionMatrix(factor(predictions,levels=c(0,1)), factor(true,c(0,1)), positive = "1")

sensitivity <- conf_mat$byClass["Sensitivity"]
specificity <- conf_mat$byClass["Specificity"]
ppv <- conf_mat$byClass["Pos Pred Value"]
balanced_acc <- conf_mat$byClass["Balanced Accuracy"]

roc_obj <- roc(true, as.numeric(prob))
auc_val <- auc(roc_obj)

print(paste("Sens:",sensitivity))
print(paste("Spec:",specificity))
print(paste("PPV:",ppv))
print(paste("Bal_acc",balanced_acc))

print(paste("AUC:",auc_val))

print(paste("Profit:",p))
```

# 5. PAC and Farness

```{r}

# Predicted probabilities (Lasso)
prob_test <- as.numeric(predict(cv_lasso, newx = x_test, s = "lambda.min", type = "response"))

# Compute PAC
PAC_test <- pmin(prob_test, 1 - prob_test)

#Compute Farness
# Standardize using TRAIN stats
X_train_scaled <- as.matrix(scale(x_train))
X_test_scaled  <- scale(
  x_test,
  center = attr(X_train_scaled, "scaled:center"),
  scale  = attr(X_train_scaled, "scaled:scale")
)
X_test_scaled <- as.matrix(X_test_scaled)

# Make sure Response is consistently coded for centroid selection
y_train_fac <- if (is.numeric(train$Response)) factor(train$Response, levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No","Yes")) else factor(train$Response)
y_test_fac  <- if (is.numeric(test$Response))  factor(test$Response,  levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No","Yes")) else factor(test$Response)

# Class centroids (in standardized space)
centroid_yes <- colMeans(X_train_scaled[y_train_fac == "Yes", , drop = FALSE])
centroid_no  <- colMeans(X_train_scaled[y_train_fac == "No",  , drop = FALSE])

# Farness: distance to own-class centroid
farness_test <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(X_test_scaled)), function(i) {
  if (y_test_fac[i] == "Yes") {
    sqrt(sum((X_test_scaled[i, ] - centroid_yes)^2))
  } else {
    sqrt(sum((X_test_scaled[i, ] - centroid_no)^2))
  }
})

# Plot PAC vs Farness visualization
pac_farness_df <- data.frame(
  PAC = PAC_test,
  Farness = farness_test,
  TrueClass = y_test_fac
)

ggplot(pac_farness_df, aes(x = Farness, y = PAC, color = TrueClass)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "PAC vs Farness – Lasso Logistic Regression",
    x = "Farness",
    y = "Probability of Alternative Class (PAC)"
  )
```
